title: Stream Compactification: SDK UX & Tool Runbook (draft)
body:
SUMMARY
This is a working runbook / design sketch exploring a compact, latency-focused streaming surface for the Hosted API SDKs that prioritizes:
- minimal client-side framing and memory (mobile/edge first)
- predictable latency SLOs under token pressure
- explicit lightweight semantics for tool-calls and structured output that are cheap to parse and resumable
- developer ergonomics for reactive frameworks (React, Vue, Solid) and server runtimes (Node, Deno, Go)

High-level proposal in one sentence: define a compact frame protocol + lightweight SDK primitives that expose 'quality anchors' and 'tool leases' so clients can make cost/latency tradeoffs deterministically and resume partial outputs without re-running full inference.

Why this?
- Current streaming prototypes focus on rich partial output but leave clients guessing when content is stable enough to commit or to call external services.
- Large mobile apps need small memory and cheap reconnection behavior.
- Observability and local replay are hard when frames mix partial tokens, JSON text shards, and tool-call manifests.

GOALS
- A minimal wire format ("compact frames") that fits on poor networks and provides small typed headers for quick routing and parsing.
- SDK primitives that are: low-footprint, promise-based (JS), async-iterators-friendly, and have first-class suspend/resume semantics.
- Clear guarantees for tool-calls: idempotency keys, optional preflight, and a short-lived tool-lease TTL to reduce duplicate invocations on reconnection.
- Structured output "projection" mechanism: clients can request shape filtering to reduce payload size and parsing cost.

NON-GOALS
- Full fidelity schema enforcement server-side (we provide projection + best-effort validation only).
- Large changes to the core streaming runtime (we add packing/labels and small router hooks).

KEY CONCEPTS (NEW)
1) Compact frame: single-line header + payload (binary or text). Header fields: frame-type, seq, session-id, quality-anchor, lease-hint. Example: "F:SEQ=231;S=abcd;Q=0.82;L=tool:wiki:30\n<payload>"
   - frame-type: T (tokens), S (structure snapshot), C (call-tool), M (meta/checkpoint).
   - quality-anchor: float 0..1, heuristic score indicating server confidence in partial output correctness. Useful for clients that make early decisions.
   - lease-hint: lightweight hint like "tool:<id>:<ttl>s" if frame contains a tool invocation prepared on-server.

2) Tool lease: server promises a short TTL for a tool invocation id so clients that reconnect can ask the server to continue monitoring rather than re-invoke immediately. Lease can be extended by heartbeat if the server supports long polling or kept minimal (default 20s).

3) Schema projection token: client can request a projection token in the initial request to indicate minimal set of fields it needs (e.g., {answer, citations}). Server still streams full tokens but emits S (structure snapshot) frames frequently which are projection-friendly. This reduces client CPU for parsing.

4) Resume-quality anchor: small deterministic checkpoints (M frames) containing hashes of key fields + final token offset. On resume, client sends last-known M frame id and server can replay from offset or rehydrate KV-cache efficiently.

SDK SURFACE SUGGESTIONS (JS-first, also sketches for other runtimes)
- createCompactStreamClient(opts) // opts: {mode: 'compact'|'rich', projection: ['answer','sources'], leasePolicy: 'auto'|'manual'}
- client.stream({prompt, sessionId, projectionToken}) => AsyncIterable<Frame>
   where Frame has simple getters: .type (string), .text(), .structure(), .toolCallInfo()
- convenience: client.on('quality', (anchor) => ...) + client.snapshot() -> returns last M frame id
- tool-call helper: client.tool.call(id, args, {idempotencyKey}) -> promise that resolves to toolResult OR toolLease

Example usage (pseudo-JS):
const c = createCompactStreamClient({mode:'compact', projection:['answer','top_url']})
for await (const f of c.stream({prompt})) {
  if (f.type === 'M' && f.quality > 0.8) commitUI(f.structure) // cheap shallow parse
  if (f.type === 'C') {
    // server indicated a potential tool run; ask for lease instead of invoking ourselves immediately
    const lease = await c.tool.claimLease(f.toolCallInfo.id)
    if (lease.claimed) scheduleLocalWork(lease)
  }
}

NOTES ON TOOL-CALL BEHAVIOR
- Preflight vs Server-side call: by default server will not call external tools on behalf of client unless explicitly allowed (privacy/cost). Instead, server can emit C frames containing tool-call manifests and a lease-hint.
- Idempotency: tool manifests include suggested idempotencyKey; SDK should expose helpers to transparently attach app-provided idempotency keys (or generate one tied to session + seq).
- Lease fallback: if client fails to claim lease before TTL, server may either execute immediately or discard depending on config. Document default as "best-effort but never auto-execute without explicit allow flag".

OBSERVABILITY + DEVTOOLING
- Token-level heatmap: surface on Console a compact visualization keyed by quality-anchor over time per session. Helps correlate quality dips with model changes.
- Frame logs: store M frames and C frames as first-class telemetry (cheaper than full token logs).
- SDK local simulator: small harness to replay S/M/C frames and allow UI teams to test reconnection/resume logic without hitting inference infra.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (MVP)
- Compact frames sent end-to-end with seq ordering and at least M frames every 1s for long-running responses (>2s).
- SDK prototype (JS) exposes stream iterator and tool-lease claim API.
- Console surfaces session-level quality-anchor timeline and tool-lease events.
- Reconnect test: client can resume within 2s and pick up from last M frame id without repeating tool invocations when lease active.

METRICS TO TRACK
- Percentage of client resumes that use lease vs re-invoke external tool
- Average bytes/frame for compact mode vs rich mode
- P95 resume latency after network drop
- Correlation of quality-anchor < 0.6 with downstream user rejection events (if available)

OPEN QUESTIONS / DISCUSSION ITEMS
- TTL sizing: mobile networks vary, default 20s may be too short for some apps. Provide app-level knob.
- How to compute quality-anchor? Candidate: a small ensemble of token-level logit gap + schema-likelihood. Need applied-ml to propose fast approximation.
- Should console show predicted cost impact when client enables projection? (helpful for PLG)
- Security: do we allow server-side tool execution for hosted-api customers by default? probably off; need enterprise flag.

ROLLOUT PLAN (PHASED)
- Phase 0 (prototype): wire-format + JS SDK experiment in dev environment, simulate with harness. (2 sprints)
- Phase 1 (beta): opt-in for specific customers, Console telemetry + lease visualization, preflight tooling documentation. (1 month)
- Phase 2 (GA): support for server-side optional execution, projection-by-default for small clients, SDKs for Python/Go. (quarter)

ACTION ITEMS (people + next steps)
- Maya: prototype JS SDK iterator + lease claim helper (due 2024-11-29)
- Samir: write unit tests for resume logic and size simulations (due 2024-12-06)
- Leo: coord with Applied ML for a fast quality-anchor heuristic; propose metric in Confluence (linked) (due 2024-12-03)
- Product: draft UX copy for Console quality timeline and lease events.

NOTES TO SELF (rough ideas, keep)
- Consider a compact binary form for mobile (protobuf-lite) but keep text-frame fallback for debugging and proxies.
- Think about 'prefetch tipping points' where client switches from speculative local execution to server tool execution based on battery/latency metrics.
- Explore 'progressive projection' where client can request more fields mid-stream if quality-anchor crosses threshold.

REFERENCES / LINKS
- jira:HOSTEDAPI-892 (stream-resume-tests)
- confluence:HOSTED-STREAM-RUNBOOK-247
- github:pull/3123 (compact frame prototype)

END
